note.text: Once a singleton lights, that object is a nexiom and the machine needs one. A dark set then contains no nexioms—drop every member. The partner is somewhere in the objects never shown dark; a lit group only proves at least one nexiom is inside, and a known nexiom already explains it. With candidates left and tests scarce, split them: test half. Light means the partner is in that half; dark means it is in the other half. Do not retest confirmed singles or confirmed non-nexioms. If one candidate remains, that is the partner.
